queueGate.rule: Brief: poll GET /queue until it has been EMPTY for 10 consecutive minutes before queueing the one render job (this job would otherwise block the shared GPU for 60-90 minutes).
queueGate.outcome: NOT MET. Monitored continuously for roughly 50 minutes (2026-09-22 ~13:50-14:47 EDT); the queue was never empty for more than ~110 seconds at a stretch.
queueGate.evidence: Two other tracks were actively and visibly using the GPU back-to-back the whole time: an ACE-Step music-audition workflow (public/audio/candidates + D:/Tools/ComfyUI/output/pyrefly-ace, which grew from 34 to 62+ rendered .flac candidates across several seed/denoise/model-variant sweeps while this pass watched), immediately followed by an IPAdapter-based image generation job (CheckpointLoaderSimple/IPAdapterAdvanced/ImageBatch graph, seen running via GET /queue right after the audio track stopped producing new files).
queueGate.decision: Did not queue the render. Forcing a 60-90 minute job into that queue would have stalled two other in-progress tracks, which is exactly what the 10-minute gate exists to prevent. No GPU time was spent on the actual render or VRAM probe beyond the single few-second VAE-floor validation above.
queueGate.nextStep: Re-run the same wait-for-empty-10-minutes check, then `node tools/gen/video-flf.mjs render idle-blinks --seed 1` (defaults now apply the round-3 fix: 24fps, length 97, RepeatImageBatch end anchor).
